To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the redox potential of the cytoplasm in the liver is determined by the adenine nucleotide phosphorylation potential and that this potential, in turn, is determined by the energy state of the liver.

the [ATP] and [ADP] concentrations in the cytoplASM are controlled by a mechanism that is essentially identical with the mechanism that controls the [ATP], [ADP] and [P(i)] concentrations in the mitochondria.

the redox ratio [NAD(+)+NADP(+)]/[NADDH+NADPH] in the cytoplASM is linked to the phosphorylation state [ATP]/ [ADP][H(2)PO(4)2] in the cytoSOL, and that the ratio [ATPA]/[ADP] in the cytosol is linked to the ratio [ATPC]/[ADP](P) in the mitochondria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the equilibrium relationships between the NAD and the ATP-ADP-P(i) systems in rat liver.
a study of the equilibrium relations between the two major phosphorylating systems of the cell, the cytoplasm and the mitochondria.
the interrelations between the adenine nucleotide and the nicotinamide nucleotide systems in the cytoplasp of the rat liver cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the [NADH] concentration in the cytoplasma is a direct function of the [AT(P)/[HPO(4)](2-)] ratio, and is independent of the [N AD(+)] concentration.
the redox and phosphorylation states of the adenine and nicotinadine nucleotides are linked in such a way that the [NAD(+)]/[NADH] and [ATP]/ [ADP][H2PO(4)] ratios are approximately equal.
the ratio [ATPD]/[ADP]HPO(4)(2-)] is the major factor in controlling the redox state, and that the redox ratio, in turn, is an important factor in controlling the phosphorylation state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the [ATP] and [NAD(+)], and to a lesser extent [ADP] and [HPO(4)(2-)], are the primary determinants of the redox state in the cytoplASM.
the [ATP] and [NAD(+)], as well as the [NADH]/[NAD(+)] ratio, are all linked to the nutritional status and the [ATP][NAD(+)]/(ADP][NADH]) ratio is a good index of the nutritional state.
in the liver cell the ratio [ATPDH]/[ADP] is maintained at a constant value of 0.8 by the action of the adenine kinase and that this constant is the basis of the constancy of the ratio [ATD]/[ADP].
The main takeaway from our work is that
the redox ratio of the NADH/NAD+ couple in the cytosol is linked to, if not directly controlled by, the ATP/ADP ratio.
the redox ratio of NAD+ to NADH is controlled by the ratio of ATP to ADP.
, when the [ATP][ADP][H(2)PO(4)(2-)] ratio is low, the NADH/NAD(+) ratio is low, and the [NAD(+)]/[NADH] is low, and this is the case in many disease states.
